- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast, particularly if recent price is trending up.
- Overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., >75% from prior day) are common; cap forecast at +10–15% above peak for 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 18-day moving average, adjust downward; if below, adjust upward if sentiment is bullish.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overreact to short-term sentiment; dampen momentum by 15–20% if sentiment is volatile or mixed.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive within 3–5 days, model often misses the reversal; adjust forecast upward by 5–10% on next day.
